title: Changes to a city transport network

lines.t: Attention, all passengers. This is an announcement from City Transit about important changes to our network, which start on the first Monday of next month.
Let us begin with the buses. Route twelve will no longer run along Station Road, because the road will be closed for repairs for about five months.
Instead, it will pass through Market Square, and the journey will take around six minutes longer.
Route seven, which many of you know, will be withdrawn completely.
Passengers who used it should take the new route twenty-seven, which follows almost the same path but also stops at the central library.
Now the trams. Line B will be extended by three stops, so that it finally reaches the university hospital.
Trams will run every ten minutes during the day, instead of every twelve.
These changes should connect the hospital with the city centre, which residents have requested for many years, and they should also make daily journeys faster.
At night, we are improving the service for people who work late or go out in the evening.
On Fridays and Saturdays, night buses will run every thirty minutes instead of every hour. Please note that this applies only to those two nights.
Turning to fares. A single ticket stays at two dollars fifty, so there is no change there.
However, the day pass will rise from seven dollars to eight dollars, the first increase in four years.
There is good news for students. The discount card will now give thirty percent off all tickets.
We had announced twenty-five percent last month, but the city council agreed to a larger reduction.
Finally, cycling. Bicycle hire stations will open at twenty tram stops, and the first thirty minutes are free for card holders.
To plan your journey, update our app, which shows the new routes from today.
Information desks at the central station will also be open until nine every evening this week, and staff will be happy to help. Thank you for listening.

qs.q: Why is route twelve changing its path?
o: A road will be closed for repairs
A new tram line is being built
qs.why: طريق المحطة سيُغلق للإصلاح نحو خمسة أشهر.

qs.why: الخط السابع ألغي وحلّ محله الخط السابع والعشرون.

qs.why: سيُمدّد الخط بثلاث محطات.

qs.q: On Fridays and Saturdays, night buses will run every ___ minutes.
qs.why: كل نصف ساعة بدل كل ساعة.

qs.q: The price of a single ticket will go up.
qs.why: التذكرة المفردة تبقى بسعر دولارين وخمسين سنتاً.

qs.q: What will the new price of the day pass be?
qs.why: سيرتفع من سبعة إلى ثمانية دولارات.

qs.why: وافق المجلس على تخفيض أكبر من الإعلان السابق.

qs.q: Bicycle hire stations will open at ___ tram stops.
qs.why: عشرون محطة ترام.

lines.t: Come in, both of you. I have read your draft proposal on social media use and sleep, and I think it has real potential.
Thank you, Dr Hall. We were not sure about the title. Is it too long?
The title is fine. My concern is the research question. At the moment you ask whether social media harms students' health, which is far too broad.
So we should focus on sleep only?
Exactly, Ben. Something like, how does evening social media use affect the sleep of first-year students? That is specific and measurable.
That makes sense. We planned to survey two hundred students. Is that enough?
More than enough for a project this size. A hundred and twenty would be realistic, and you would still have time to analyse the data properly.
Okay. I suggested using wearable sleep trackers, but Layla thought they would cost too much.
Yes, they were about eighty pounds each. Instead, we would use a questionnaire and a two-week sleep diary.
A sensible compromise. Diaries are not perfect, because people forget, but they are acceptable for an undergraduate study. Just make sure you explain the limitation.
Do we need ethical approval?
Definitely, and before you collect any data. The committee usually takes three weeks, so submit the form as soon as you can.
And the literature review? How many studies do we need?
At least ten, published in the last five years. Layla, you mentioned some research on teenagers.
That is useful as background, but your main sources should be about university students.
I will look for more this weekend.
Good. Your topic matters to many students, and the university may even use your findings, so please take the work seriously. Now, who will write which section?
I can write the methodology, and Layla will do the introduction.
Fine. The final proposal is due next Friday at noon. Please send it to me by email on Thursday evening, so I can check it first.
We will do that. Thank you very much.

qs.q: What is the tutor's main concern about the draft?
o: The research question is too broad
qs.why: السؤال البحثي واسع جداً.

qs.q: The tutor wants the study to focus on students' ___.
qs.why: اقترح التركيز على النوم فقط.

qs.q: How many students does the tutor think is a realistic sample?
qs.why: العدد الواقعي في رأيه مئة وعشرون.

qs.q: Why do the students decide not to use wearable trackers?
o: Students would refuse to wear them
qs.why: كلّفة الجهاز حوالي ثمانين جنيهاً.

qs.q: The tutor says the students should explain the limits of sleep diaries.
qs.why: طلب شرح القيد لأن الناس ينسون.

qs.why: اللجنة تحتاج عادة ثلاثة أسابيع.

qs.q: The literature review needs at least ___ studies.
qs.why: عشر دراسات على الأقل من السنوات الخمس الأخيرة.

qs.q: Who will write the methodology section?
qs.why: المتحدث الثالث (بن) سيكتب المنهجية.

lines.t: So, Jake, we need to decide how to collect the data for our library project. I made a list of three methods.
Great. Start with the online questionnaire, because that is what I expected we would choose.
The main advantages are cost and speed. We could build it for free and get answers within days. The disadvantage is the response rate.
My cousin ran one at work and only about ten percent replied.
And the people who reply are often the ones with strong opinions, so the results might not represent everyone.
Right, that is called self-selection. Second option, telephone interviews. Response is much better, perhaps forty-five percent, and the interviewer can explain unclear questions.
But phone calls cost money, and these days many people never answer a number they do not know. We only have three hundred dollars in the budget.
True. Third, face-to-face surveys outside the library. We would get rich, detailed answers, and people can show us things on a map or a list.
That sounds the most useful, but it takes much longer. Each interview would last at least fifteen minutes, and we would stand outside for hours.
There is also the risk of interviewer bias. People may give polite answers because someone is looking at them.
Good point. What if we combine methods? The online questionnaire could be our main source, and we add twenty face-to-face interviews to understand the reasons behind the numbers.
I like that. We could offer a prize draw to encourage people to answer the questionnaire. A fifty dollar voucher, perhaps.
Hmm, I am not sure. A prize might attract people who do not use the library at all, and they would just click through quickly.
Maybe we should simply ask the library to advertise it on its website.
Fair enough. Let us do that instead. And before we launch, we should test the questions with ten friends.
Yes, a pilot study. If anything confuses them, we will rewrite it.
Perfect. I will draft the questionnaire tonight, and you contact the library manager.

qs.q: What are the main advantages of an online questionnaire?
qs.why: رخيص وسريع لكن نسبة الاستجابة ضعيفة.

qs.q: Only about ___ percent of people answered the online survey at the cousin's work.
qs.why: نسبة الرد حوالي عشرة بالمئة.

qs.q: What is the problem with self-selection?
o: Replies come mainly from people with strong opinions
qs.why: المجيبون غالباً أصحاب آراء قوية فلا تمثل النتائج الجميع.

qs.q: Why do they doubt telephone interviews?
o: They cost money and many people ignore unknown numbers
qs.why: التكلفة وعدم الرد على أرقام مجهولة.

qs.q: The budget for the project is ___ dollars.
qs.why: الميزانية ثلاثمئة دولار.

qs.q: Face-to-face interviews may lead people to give polite answers.
qs.why: هذا هو تحيّز القائم بالمقابلة.

qs.q: They decide to add ___ face-to-face interviews.
qs.why: عشرون مقابلة لفهم الأسباب وراء الأرقام.

qs.q: What do they decide about the prize draw?
o: Ask the library to advertise the survey instead
Offer a prize only to library members
qs.why: رفضا الجائزة وفضّلا الإعلان في موقع المكتبة.

title: Planning a presentation on renewable energy

lines.t: Right, let us plan our renewable energy presentation. We have twelve minutes in total, and then three minutes for questions.
Should we cover every type of renewable energy?
No, that would be too much. I suggest solar, wind, and then storage, because storage is the biggest challenge.
What about nuclear power? Some people call it clean energy.
It is low carbon, but it is not renewable, and our brief says renewable sources only. So we leave it out.
Fair. I will mention it in one sentence at most if someone asks.
How should we divide the work? I would like to take wind, because I read a good report about offshore wind farms.
Perfect, Sam. I will do the introduction and solar. Priya, can you take storage and the conclusion?
Sure. I can explain batteries and why the sun does not always shine when we need electricity.
For visuals, I think we need a map showing the main wind farm areas. Pictures work better than lots of words.
Agreed. For solar, I want a graph showing how the price of panels has fallen over the last ten years. It is a very clear trend.
And a case study might help. There is a village that put solar panels on the school roof and now saves money on its electricity bills.
Nice. Keep the case study to one slide. The professor said no more than ten slides, with very little text.
So that is three slides each, plus a title slide.
Exactly. When can we practise? I am free on Thursday afternoon.
I have a lab until three, but after four o'clock would be good.
Same for me. Shall we book a room in the library?
I will do it online tonight. Our presentation is on Monday at nine thirty, so we need at least one full rehearsal.
And we should time ourselves. Last time my group ran two minutes over, and we lost marks.
Good advice. Let us send our slides to each other by Wednesday evening.

qs.q: The presentation must last ___ minutes in total.
qs.why: اثنتا عشرة دقيقة ثم ثلاث دقائق للأسئلة.

qs.q: Why do they leave out nuclear power?
o: It is too difficult to explain
qs.why: التعليمات تطلب مصادر متجددة فقط.

qs.q: Which topic will Sam take?
qs.why: سام يريد أن يتناول طاقة الرياح.

qs.q: What visual will be used for the wind section?
qs.why: خريطة لأهم مناطق مزارع الرياح.

qs.q: The solar graph will show that panel prices have risen.
qs.why: الرسم يوضح أن الأسعار انخفضت خلال عشر سنوات.

qs.q: The professor allows no more than ___ slides.
qs.why: عشر شرائح كحد أقصى.

qs.q: When will the group rehearse?
qs.why: أحدهم لديه مختبر حتى الثالثة فاتفقوا بعد الرابعة.

qs.q: Priya says a group of hers lost marks for going over time.
qs.why: تأخرت مجموعتها دقيقتين فخسرت درجات.

title: Feedback on a first essay draft

lines.t: Thanks for coming, Karim. I have read your draft essay on whether public transport should be free, and overall I was impressed.
Really? I was worried it was a mess.
Not at all. The structure is clear and your examples are vivid, especially the one about the city that made buses free for pensioners.
Thank you. What should I improve?
Let us start with the introduction. It is nearly four hundred words, which is almost a third of the whole essay. Also, there is no clear thesis statement.
I thought the thesis was in the last sentence.
It is hinted at, but a reader should know your position immediately. Try one clear sentence, then move on.
Okay. And the body paragraphs?
Paragraphs one, two and four work well. Paragraph three is about the cost of building roads, which is interesting but not really relevant, so I suggest deleting it.
That would also help with the length. I counted fourteen hundred words, and the limit is twelve hundred.
Yes, so you need to cut about two hundred words. Sorry, I said three hundred earlier, but two hundred is correct, since the references do not count.
Right. What about my sources?
This is the weakest point. Several of your sources are blogs and news websites. For a university essay, you should use academic journals or official reports.
Where do I find those?
Start with the library database. If you search for urban transport policy, you will find plenty. The librarian can also show you how.
Is it all right to write I think in the essay?
Better to avoid it. Use phrases such as it can be argued that or the evidence suggests. It sounds more academic.
Understood. And the conclusion?
It repeated your main points well, but it added a new argument about air pollution. A conclusion should never introduce new ideas.
I will fix that. When is the final deadline?
Wednesday of next week, at five. Come back before then if you want me to look at the new introduction.

qs.q: What does the tutor praise about the essay?
qs.why: أثنى على وضوح البناء وحيوية الأمثلة.

qs.q: The introduction is nearly ___ words long.
qs.why: المقدمة قرابة أربعمئة كلمة.

qs.q: What is wrong with the introduction apart from its length?
o: It has no clear thesis statement
qs.why: لا توجد عبارة أطروحة واضحة.

qs.q: Which paragraph does the tutor suggest deleting?
qs.why: الفقرة الثالثة عن تكلفة بناء الطرق غير ذات صلة.

qs.q: Karim needs to cut about ___ words.
qs.why: صحّح المدرّس رقمه من ثلاثمئة إلى مئتين.

qs.q: What is the problem with Karim's sources?
o: Several are blogs and news websites
There are too few of them
qs.why: عليه استخدام المجلات الأكاديمية والتقارير الرسمية.

qs.q: The tutor recommends using the phrase I think in academic essays.
qs.why: نصح بتجنبها واستعمال عبارات مثل it can be argued that.

qs.q: What is wrong with the conclusion?
o: It does not repeat the main points
qs.why: أضافت حجة جديدة عن تلوث الهواء.
